groups.text: It is currently 13 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

South Korean President Jae Myung Lee is meeting with NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners at this week’s AI Summit in San Francisco. The president, joined by top researchers and business leaders, aims to chart Korea's progress toward becoming a global center for AI innovation. This push follows a visit to Korea last month by NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. As part of the effort to expand national infrastructure, NVIDIA and the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology announced a joint AI research lab in Seoul. Dedicated to advancing agentic AI, this is the first joint lab between a Korean university and a global technology company. The collaboration combines KAIST scientific talent with NVIDIA Nemotron open models and AI Cloud computing. On the eve of the summit, Huang also held a dinner in Woodside, California, with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won and teams from SK Telecom and SK hynix.

Richard Carapaz has claimed a solo victory in the eighteenth stage of the Tour de France. The Ecuadorian rider launched a decisive attack late in the race to leave his competitors behind, finishing forty-five seconds ahead of Mauro Schmid from Switzerland and Matteo Jorgenson from the United States. The peloton now prepares for another mountain stage on Friday featuring over three thousand meters of positive elevation gain. Separately, Uzbekistan is considering a shift in how its tourism industry handles extreme summer heat. A draft presidential decree proposes introducing siesta hours for hotels, museums, and catering facilities to protect workers and tourists from high temperatures. Under this plan, businesses could close during the hottest part of the day, from one until five in the afternoon, while extending their overall operating hours from seven in the morning until eleven at night.

In Turkey, former CHP leader Özgür Özel is founding his own political party after a court ordered his removal from the opposition's leadership. This follows a violent confrontation in May when Turkish special forces used tear gas and water cannons to clear the CHP headquarters in Ankara. Special has claimed his only fault was leading the CHP to defeat the ruling AKP party in the March 2024 local elections, where the opposition took control of 14 major cities including Istanbul. Up to 90 members of parliament may now join Özel's new party. Meanwhile, in North Wales, the government has activated crisis management arrangements to combat widespread wildfires. Satellite data from NASA and BBC Verify show that approximately 951 hectares of the Rhinogydd mountains in Gwynedd have burned. A specialist firefighting helicopter is being deployed to the region as heat signatures are also detected in Powys, Torfaen, and Flintshire.

Reports of a cabinet reshuffle are sparking debate over the future of German governance and social spending. Health Minister Warken is expected to become the new head of the Chancellery, a move the Wirtschaftswoche attributes to her loyalty to the Chancellor and her leadership of the CDU's Women's Union. The Augsburger Allgemeine notes that Warken proved she could handle political backlash by pushing through savings in statutory health insurance. Her successor, CDU General Secretary Carsten Linnemann, lacks government experience but is known for advocating cuts to the welfare state. While some see this as a strategic move, the Berliner Morgenpost warns of risks. The paper suggests Merz is moving Warken before her work is finished, leaving the most difficult challenges facing the nursing care system unresolved.

Russian forces launched more than ten drone and artillery attacks across two districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. Oleksandr Hanzha, the head of the regional military administration, reports that strikes in the Nikopol district damaged a gas station, an apartment building, and private homes. In the Kryvyi Rih district, Russian forces struck the Novopillia community, which sparked a fire. These attacks follow a strike on a food processing enterprise in Pavlohrad that killed three people and injured 28 others. Shifting to technical research, Andrei Cristian Popescu and his colleagues are diagnosing adaptive depth in looped Transformers. They found that fixed-prior depth supervision creates difficulty-aware trajectories without needing an input-dependent halting policy. Their study across synthetic tasks and Ouro checkpoints suggests that simple post-hoc confidence readouts often match or outperform learned linear and MLP gates, addressing how these models manage test-time computation through recurrent blocks.

Thai authorities are investigating a network that allegedly used Thai men as fake fathers to secure citizenship for foreign children. Police and the DOPA N.I.C.E. task force have identified 1,483 suspected fraudulent birth registrations linked to eight hospitals. The probe began after the arrest of a Chinese national accused of laundering over 70 billion baht for a scam network; investigators discovered his three children held Thai nationality despite both parents being Chinese. Recent raids at a private hospital in Bangkok’s Rama IX area led to four arrests, including two men posing as fathers and a Chinese couple. Since July 9, police have arrested 37 suspects, including 16 fake fathers and 13 Chinese mothers. Separately, in sports, Ecuadorian Richard Carapaz won Stage 18 of the Tour de France with a solo breakaway. He finished 45 seconds ahead of American Matteo Jorgenson and Switzerland’s Mauro Schmid.

Armed attacks in Ethiopia's East Arsi Zone have left more than 53 Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Christians dead. Reports indicate that violence beginning in late May and continuing into June targeted the districts of Aseko, Sherka, Honkolo Wabe, and Munesa, where attackers burned homes and churches and displaced hundreds of civilians. These attacks highlight a volatile environment where Amhara people are targeted for their ethnic identity and faith, often fueled by the misconception that all Orthodox Christians are Amhara. Separately, in the field of financial machine learning, researcher Marcos Florencio has proposed a new method to reduce subjectivity in portfolio construction. The approach uses neural predicates as a probabilistic mechanism to generate investor views within the Black-Litterman model. By processing structured financial analysis through a compositional hierarchy, the system maps data to market stances and uncertainty estimates, allowing any specific portfolio weight to be traced back to its underlying data source.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with temperatures between 18 and 22 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 09:00, FW: Soofi - Evaluation at Microsoft Teams Meeting, at 13:00, NAS Brainstorm, at 17:00, Friday beer & Cocktails, and at 19:00, Höfische.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
